subject: general
question: A ______ performance begins with the kelikottu, calling the audience to attention followed by the todayam.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kathakali

 
 
• Kathakali derives its name from the words ‘Katha’ meaning story, and ‘Kali’ meaning drama.
 
• It is a wonderful combination of music, dance, and drama.
 
• It is presented in the temple precincts after dusk falls.
 
• A **Kathakali **performance is heralded by the Kelikottu or the beating of drums to the accompaniment of the Chengila (gong).
 
• It is over 300 years old. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Kathakali

 
 
• Kathakali dance originated in** Kerala.**
 
• It is one of the **eight classical dances in India **recognised bySangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• It is closely related to Koodiyattam (Sanskrit drama tradition) and other ancient martial arts performances also. 
 
• Most of the Kathakali recitals are a grand representation of the eternal conflict between good and evil.
 
• It draws its themes from the stories narrated in the epics and the Puranas.
 
 
• It is also called the ‘ballad of the east
 
 
 
• The Indigenous Music of Kerala 'Sopana Sangeetham ' is used in Kathakali.
 
• The instruments used in the Kathakali are Chenda (a type of drum), Madhalam (a long cylindrical drum), Chengila ( gong), and Ilathalam (an instrument similar to a cymbal). Sometimes Idakka (a type of small drum) is also used. 
 
• Gestures are perhaps the crown jewel of the entire dance drama.
 
• Kathakali is remarkable in the representation of the rasas through movements of the eye and eyebrows, through which the story is conveyed.
 
• **Nine important facial expressions called ‘Navarasas**’ are taught to convey** different emotions.**
